title: Trace-to-metric joiner with debug sampling and backfill capability
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Implement a service and pipeline components that reliably join sampled traces (OTel) with per-request metrics (Prometheus/OTLP generated KPIs) for deterministic latency/error attribution and on-demand backfill. Enable a lightweight debug-sampling toggle to collect high-fidelity exemplars and trace links for a small percentage of requests without blowing up metric cardinality or downstream storage costs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministically joinable key is produced for each request by runtime (request_id or hashed fingerprint) and propagated to spans, metrics, and logs
Exemplar-level links: Prometheus exemplars contain trace/span references for debug-sampled requests and are searchable in the Console traces view
Backfill pipeline: we can reprocess past traces from the trace-store and emit synthesized per-request metrics that reconcile with existing KPIs for historical attribution
Cardinality guard rules prevent label explosion during debug sampling and backfill (configurable tenant thresholds)
End-to-end tests validate join correctness across common failure modes (partial spans, span redaction, multi-segment requests)
Dashboard panels (latency breakdown and error attribution) show trace-joined metrics and allow toggling between live and backfilled data
technical_notes: Join key design: prefer 128-bit request_fingerprint; fallback to (tenant_id, route, proxied_request_id) when unavailable
Instrumentation: SDK changes required in inference runtime to attach request_fingerprint to OTEL Resource/Span attributes and to metrics envelopes (OTLP / Prometheus exemplars)
Sampling: provide two mechanisms — lightweight probabilistic debug sampling for live linkage; deterministic on-demand sample by request ID for reproductions
Backfill approach: rehydrate traces from trace-store (Bigtable/S3), run a reprocessor that emits OTLP-metrics with original timestamps, and write to the metric ingest path with a backfill tag
Cardinality controls: use label allowlists, truncate high-cardinality attributes, and bucket rare label values under __other__ for backfilled metrics
Storage/cost: backfill emits to an isolated retention stream to avoid inflating production billing; per-tenant quotas enforced
Observability UX: Console will resolve exemplar trace links and fall back to a trace summary when full span payloads are unavailable
Security: ensure backfilled trace data respects tenant isolation and PII redaction rules
progress_updates: 2025-09-15: Ticket created. Initial scoping with runtime and telemetry teams. Identified request_fingerprint as primary join key.
2025-09-22: Prototype SDK patch landed for attaching request_fingerprint to spans and exemplars. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/421

2025-09-29: Spike completed for trace rehydration pipeline; able to re-emit OTLP-metrics from historical traces at ~2k reqs/s in dev cluster. Internal notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Trace+Backfill+Spike
2025-10-03: Design review with Privacy & Security. Agreed on PII redaction and tenant-scoped backfill streams. Security review checklist created.
2025-10-06: Implementing cardinality guard heuristics and exemplar indexing. Working on metric ingest connector changes to accept backfill-tagged metrics.
decisions: Use request_fingerprint as canonical join key; do not rely on sampling-only identifiers
Backfill path will write to a separate Kafka topic (metric-backfill) with explicit retention and billing isolation
Enable debug-sampling by default at 0.1% per-tenant; allow customer override up to configured limit
Truncate unrecognized high-cardinality labels to 64 chars and hash-canonicalize when necessary
